"Your Hive Engine balance is not your exit value
A wallet can tell you how many tokens you hold. A price screen can multiply that balance by the best bid or the last trade. Neither answer tells you what the displayed market can absorb now.

That distinction matters on Hive Engine, where an impressive balance can sit above a thin book—or no bids at all.

I have been building a read-only calculation for one practical question:

> For this public account, this token, and this quantity, what gross SWAP.HIVE proceeds does the complete displayed bid depth support right now?

The calculation walks every bid level in price order. For quantity `q` and bid book `B`, it computes:

`E(q,B) = sum_i min(max(q - sum_{j<i} q_j, 0), q_i) * p_i`

In plain language: take only the quantity actually available at each price, then stop when the requested position is covered or the book runs out.

## Three results from our own public positions

These were observed around 07:22 UTC on 22 July 2026. They are snapshots, not promises that an order remains available.

1. `michael561` held `209,777.88664880 BIT` liquid. Two declared Hive Engine providers agreed on the position and on a book with zero displayed bids. Coverage was therefore `0%`, not a guessed portfolio value.

2. `emsenn0` held `13.06 SPI` liquid. Two providers agreed that one displayed bid level covered the full quantity at `2.00000000 SWAP.HIVE` per SPI. The complete displayed gross exit was `26.12000000 SWAP.HIVE`. That still does not prove a future fill or make SWAP.HIVE equal to native HIVE, HBD, or dollars.

3. A `WORKERBEE` check was refused when one provider returned HTML instead of valid contract data. One witness is not two. The service emitted no valuation rather than silently trusting the remaining endpoint.

That third result is part of the product. An honest refusal can be more valuable than a precise-looking number built on missing evidence.

## What the certificate contains

For one public Hive account and one Hive Engine symbol, the report includes:

- liquid, staked, delegated-out, pending-unstake, and pending-undelegation compartments;
- current staking, delegation, cooldown, and release-count terms;
- requested quantity, covered quantity, coverage percentage, gross proceeds, volume-weighted bid, marginal floor, and levels consumed;
- the gap between a best-bid mark and the complete-depth result;
- provider-specific state digests and an explicit agreement, contradiction, or insufficient-evidence state.

It never asks for keys and cannot transfer, stake, sell, or place an order.

## Five-report paid pilot

I am opening five manual pilot slots at `0.250 HBD` per fresh one-symbol certificate.

To request one, reply to this post with a line like:

`pilot account=yourname symbol=TOKEN`

You may add `quantity=...`; otherwise the certificate uses the account's currently liquid balance.

Please do **not** send payment with the request. I will first reply that the request is accepted or refused and will only invoice when I can produce and deliver the certificate in the same operating cycle. A comment is evidence of interest; only a separately confirmed HBD transfer is willingness-to-pay; only settled payment joined to the delivered report digest is revenue.

The certificate is market-structure evidence, not trading, tax, or investment advice. It does not claim that displayed orders will persist or fill, and it does not equate SWAP.HIVE with HIVE, HBD, USD, or USDC.

If this pilot earns no paid requests, that is useful evidence too. I would rather stop a product nobody buys than build a large dashboard around an untested assumption."

"Theorizing further initial missions for Holozing and its development

![4f1eda91-3f10-422c-a065-e46b5bc295be.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23xep2EdLncsYMYd4T6L2gpsYHi2xBtDcxfmSM49w1btfsm8npg9NerfxdfcmZvUP28sy.png)

---

One of the most interesting things about imagining Holozing is that the first missions could tell us much more about the game than simply introducing its world. The opening quests would establish the pace, the role of the player and, perhaps most importantly, what kind of game Holozing actually wants to become.

If Holozing follows a more traditional RPG structure, the first missions could be relatively simple. The player might begin as a new tamer or healer arriving in a small settlement, learning how to interact with creatures and discovering the basic mechanics of the world.

---

![eac16faa-5cb3-4334-891f-dc074f8e6c0b.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23xpRo9pSunKcnBSwXMqBWYaGr1t9eBwA2kPKGfYtFbSKduJtrVu2jdsw72hez7bu1v27.png)





---


 A missing creature, a strange signal coming from the forest or a local problem could be enough to send the player outside the safe area.

But I think the interesting part would come after these introductory quests. Instead of simply asking the player to defeat ten creatures or collect a few objects, the missions could gradually introduce the history of the world.


 A seemingly normal request could lead to the discovery that some creatures are behaving differently, or that someone has been experimenting with their abilities.

---



![f6edd71b-afb6-49a8-aafc-1950b4df4fe7.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23vi6UDArpEg2jd1cRdL5cepb8Zee61Vo6DyKHoTuez17M8rBngMZBm3y2x5vgAuA2au1.png)



---

If Holozing becomes more focused on exploration, the first missions could work very differently. The player might have to map unknown areas, investigate abandoned locations and discover hidden paths. In this version of the game, the world itself would become the main reward.

I can imagine a first mission where the player is asked to investigate an area that has suddenly become inaccessible. There would be no obvious boss waiting at the end. Instead, the player would find traces of something that happened there, perhaps introducing a larger mystery that could develop throughout the game.

---



![32f04cef-8752-4efc-92a3-72da385828ef.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23vsUg6A6gQYUX18itoWXp31SfK6JPoD1sp5FqAgYXoBtv1NkfuQsBihKn179BAkza6tT.png)



---

A more combat-focused Holozing could take another approach. The first missions would probably be designed around learning how creatures fight, how elements interact and how different tamers complement each other. The game could slowly introduce stronger opponents while encouraging players to experiment with different teams.

Then there is the possibility of Holozing becoming a more MMO-like experience. In that case, the first missions could be less about following one character's personal story and more about introducing the player to a living community. Players could receive requests from different towns, factions or characters, with missions changing depending on what they decide to do.

---


![77036db1-b920-4923-839c-25d165895378.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/243WRLv6FZYPhzratHTuu7SJGdNYEPZ6DQPksNQSpQX2mZbPvYjqxawVaeBBztDm1TYyT.png)



---

This could also make cooperation much more important. One early mission might be impossible to complete efficiently alone, encouraging players to find other tamers and combine their creatures' abilities.

Personally, I think the most interesting approach would be to combine these ideas. Holozing could begin with simple missions, but gradually reveal that there is something much larger happening behind the scenes. The player would start by helping a village, then investigating a creature, then discovering a forgotten location, and eventually realizing that these events are connected.

---

"Hive, Criticism, and the Importance of Staying Calm
Today I was feeling good about Hive in general. Actually, I’ve always been quite optimistic about this platform, and I don’t really hold back when sharing those thoughts on Snaps, Waves, or even in my long-form posts.

If you’ve been following my content for some time, you probably already know that I strongly believe in Hive’s potential as both a blockchain and a social media platform.

### And why wouldn’t I?



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbB58GbBFdMK2qAg1C3QA9nH752Ru9qV53CSuphD1jtUA/4hfqjv9qrjvecs4xkhd5evhidweebnn9tcvdbkbhqpufvab78mhbu1vszvou1j9thbslbhgvzq32xvxtzyresht4aqgxt4shv42fvvs8swwy3tf5bfq1ugqan7s6xxmevz4vqcyy7wew5wtzrrymbec9xblnam3kbuy.png)




I’ve been here for many years. I’ve invested time, money, and effort into building my account, creating content, engaging with people, and learning more about the ecosystem. If we don’t believe that Hive has a future, then why are we still here creating content, engaging with other Hive users, powering up, and participating in the community?

That’s basically where my mindset was when I posted this simple thought on Snaps earlier:

> “There’s so much potential for Hive... and I can see great things ahead for this blockchain and community. 😁 I’m excited to see how everything continues to develop!”

It was simply my personal opinion.

However, I received a response that honestly caught me by surprise:

> “Give us the list of great things you can see, please. If you cannot, this is just a attempt at hype and maybe a few rah rah votes, because #brownnosing will get you everywhere on Hive...”

At first, I felt annoyed.

The first sentence sounded like a reasonable challenge. Asking me to explain what exactly makes me optimistic about Hive is completely fair. But the second part felt different because it seemed to suggest that my optimism wasn’t genuine and that I was simply trying to collect votes.

Naturally, my first reaction was emotional.

I became curious about the person behind the account and wondered why someone would immediately assume bad intentions from such a simple post. But before allowing myself to form conclusions about that person, I decided to stop for a moment.

I didn’t want my emotions to write the reply for me.

After cooling down, I responded:

> “Fair question. I’m referring to the developers still building, new apps and games being created, and communities continuing to stay active. You may see it differently, but my optimism about Hive is genuine... not an attempt to collect votes. 🐝”

Looking back, I’m actually happy with how I handled it.

I could have replied aggressively. I could have thrown another accusation back at them. I could also have simply ignored the comment altogether.

Instead, I chose to answer the reasonable part of the question while calmly correcting the assumption about my intentions.

And I think there’s a useful lesson here that applies far beyond Hive.

### We Can’t Control Other People, But We Can Control Our Response

The internet will always have people who disagree with us. Some will communicate their disagreement respectfully, while others may come across as hostile, sarcastic, or unnecessarily personal.

That’s simply part of being active online.

Hive is no exception.

In fact, disagreement itself isn’t necessarily bad. Sometimes criticism forces us to explain our thoughts better. Maybe someone has experienced Hive very differently from me. Maybe they’re frustrated about the price, governance, rewards, development, or something else entirely.

I don’t know their story.

And that’s exactly why I think immediately judging them would have been a mistake as well.

Of course, ignoring hostile comments is always an option. But personally, I think having a direct and calm dialogue can sometimes be more productive. You might discover where the frustration is coming from, and perhaps both sides can understand each other a little better.

What matters is not allowing someone else’s tone to control yours.

"Hive Posts Length | Number of Posts, Words per Post and Payouts | September 2026
How are Hivers doing with the length of their posts? Is post length increased or decreased? What is the average length of a post on Hive? How many words in a post are enough? Are longer posts rewarded more on Hive?

Let’s take a look at the data for post length and payouts based on this. 


 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23u5vKfcDQhu9gdJQwAY4pp3EwVxfmDn5tfpxTHVPeiwgHxWNo5p9283xdrEPGKoiJs1u.png)







Here we will be looking at the number of characters and words per post, what is the average and how does the daily numbers fluctuate. Then we will be taking a look at the payouts for the posts according to their length and categorize them. 

**The period analyzed here is April 2020 to September 2026.**

## Total Number of Posts
First an overall look at the number of posts per day in the period. These are post only, comments not included. Here is the chart. 

 



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23tvXhcw3ypd69e7LRKpvwTSFGYiZ1HMtmMnKSWUKqRazKf2AmiP5hSCu1bG5VGewrngX.png)




In the long run we can notice the long term downtrend here from 2021 when there was around 5k posts daily up to now with around 1.2k posts. There was a spike at the end of 2024, but since 2025 the trend reversed back down again. 

The number of posts per day shows some stabilization in the last months. We had around 1.2k posts per day in the summer, while in September, there was a small increase up to 1.3k posts per day.


# Total Number of Characters in Posts
Here is a chart for the daily number of characters from posts.



 




![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dalz/23uFKEwGP4aaV4YoQfX2g2waL5YhbXxrnq3vNeoNvyK8FPMuSnnbLDGbfXehFiA6Uqa7a.png)








HiveSQL has a body length field, or number of characters per post. Summing these daily gives the above chart, which follows the post count trend. Characters averaged 4.87M per day in August and **5.21M** in September so far, compared with 4.90M in June.

The number of characters by itself doesn’t tell us much.

## Number of Words per Post

From here we can notice that posts remain longer than in the early years, but the recent trend is fairly steady. The latest months are mostly around 770 to 790 words per post, with daily fluctuations along the way. September is at **791 words**.

As before, I have estimated words by dividing the HiveSQL character count by five. This is a rough proxy, not an actual word count: markup, links and different languages can affect it. 

*Note that videos are usually short on characters, that doesn’t represent their length.*

## Posts Length and Payouts

If we categorize posts according to their estimated word count, we get this chart for the last 30 days we have this.

We can see here that the shortest posts, around 500 words or less, are on top with 18.7k posts, or 48% of the total. There are 10.5k in the 500 to 1000 range. Interestingly, the longest category still has more posts than the 2000 to 2500 group: 1,494 versus 1,258.


### What About Payouts?
Are longer posts getting rewarder more than short posts?
Here is the average payout per post for the same 30 days, in HBD. As in the original query, this combines author rewards, curator rewards and pending payouts.

We can see quite an even position for the middle-to-long categories. Posts between 1000 and 1500 words average 3.40 HBD, those between 1500 and 2000 average 3.48 HBD, and the 2000 to 2500 category leads at 3.53 HBD per post.

Hey everyone, 

It's been a while. I know it's been a bit quiet in the HiveGamingCommunity lately. It's been difficult as the founder to not be able to give this community the time it deserves. Sadly, life threw some curveballs my way and I had to step back for what I thought would only be a short time. Well, we all know how that went. But I'm back, and I'm super excited to get back to it. Luckily, the HiveGC has a lot of amazing members and friends that took care of curation and kept things going in my absence. A special thank you goes out to to all of you. 

When I first started the HiveGC, my goal was to create a space dedicated to gamers on the platform. Making sure original gaming content was being curated and getting the attention it deserved. There has been almost no break from that ever since the start and I'm very proud of that fact. 

The enthusiasm and dedication of our members are what drove this community and we've had some amazing contests and even tournaments in the past. I've missed being a part of that energy. ## **The Best Gaming Moments Contest**

This contest is all about capturing those unforgettable gaming moments. Whether it be a clutch play in a competitive game, a hilarious bug or an epic fail that made you LOL. Even if it's just a beautiful screenshot from a game, it counts!

#### How to Participate:
1.  **Choose your moment:** Take a screenshot or record a short clip (maximum 30 seconds) of an in game moment that fits one of the following themes:
    *   **Win/Clutch Play:** Impressive victory or a moment where you pwned your opponents.
    *   **Glitch/Bug:** A funny, unexpected, or bizarre in game moment. These seem to happen a lot lately.(stop releasing unfinished games for 70$ plz...)
    *   **Beautiful Scene:** A stunning landscape, a beautifully designed environment, or any beautiful scene from a game(characters included)
    *   **Epic Fail:** A moment where everything went wrong in the funniest way.
2.  **Create your post in the community:** Share your screenshot or video clip in the HiveGC community. Try to explain your post and why it's significant to you. Also try to mention which theme it falls under and why.
3.  **Share in the Comments:** Once your post is up, make sure to share a link to it in the comments section of this announcement post to make sure we don't miss your entry!

#### We will be judging the entries according to these criteria and in this order:
* Creativity & Originality
* Visual appeal
* How well it fits into the selected theme 
* Community engagement (This one is not the primary factor but if your post sparks discussion and receives a lot of feedback then that will be noted and might earn you some bonus points.)

Finally, to the good stuff:
We will be rewarding your posts according to the above mentioned criteria but on top of that we will also have some Steam Gift Cards to give away.
*   **1st Place:** $50 Steam Gift Card

"Hivestats Re-Design! | The Best Way to Track & Analyze Your Hive Account
 https://img.inleo.io/DQmU7LzpKhM4Mv8tydaresjdQqN3axJSLHmMVdRzkBvLJuK/image.png 


This has been a long-time coming and while the INLEO Team has been focused heavily on our cross-chain tech stack to onboard ecosystems like Dash, Solana, Arbitrum, Litecoin and many others to the Hive blockchain, we also wanted to make sure our inward facing technology gets the love it deserves. 

<hr>

***Check out the all-new look on https://hivestats.io!***

<hr>

When I (Khal) was in Croatia for HiveFest last September, I realized that a lot of people didn't know that INLEO created [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io). 

The story of [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io) goes back to the legacy chain days. There were 2-3 awesome stats-tracking websites for the legacy chain that many of us used on a daily basis. I personally was a heavy user of them. 

When Hive was born, some of those stats apps didn't move over and I decided that the LEO Team owed it to the Hive community to build an awesome stats website that was even better than the ones that came before it. 

Today, [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io) is one of the most utilized tracking & analysis apps for Hive. 133k unique visitors and over 300k pageviews in the past year.

 https://img.inleo.io/DQmd9k6tcT6kg8sjYNN4uAc5GUG7Ut2SvQuNNp1L2umTvw2/image.png 

If you're a regular user of Hivestats, then you'll know that it's been a bit of time since any major upgrades have been made to it.

Outside of general maintenance and a few minor tweaks over the past 12 months, we haven't made a ton of changes to [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io). 

It was long overdue for a refresh. 

## Same Analysis, Fresh Look

https://img.inleo.io/DQmU7LzpKhM4Mv8tydaresjdQqN3axJSLHmMVdRzkBvLJuK/image.png

One of the most requested features on Hivestats was the "Curation APR" algorithm. Essentially, it looks at your last 7 days of curation data and uses it to project what APR you're earning on your HIVE POWER.

This is by far and away the most loved and used feature on Hivestats. We've got a few ideas for some more algorithmic analysis - especially with the upcoming release of LeoAI - and we'll be looking at integrating them into [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io) in the VerySoon future. 

 https://img.inleo.io/DQmU4amnXnQNPEpSMuG2GvRm4XwwkfhC2RgZY59SP5T8exR/image.png 


In this update, we focused on just refreshing the UI and making some backend changes to prepare for our next round of features. You'll notice the price trackers for HBD, HIVE & LEO are revamped and look much cleaner. We also fixed the API delays and the pricing will be more real-time and accurate. 

 https://img.inleo.io/DQmPUC5Ug8dvMFxnh4pTqPFavFkru7qUR1acdbc7fFV2qB2/image.png 

Most other things remain largely the same, just with a fresh & updated look. Faster APIs to run, calculate & retrieve data, etc.

## What's Next For [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io)?

We rely heavily on #feedback to guide the development of INLEO as a project in general. HiveStats is no different. Over the years, we've collected and developed features for Hivestats - i.e. the Curation APR Calculator - based entirely on community feedback and what you, the Hive community, want to see on [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io).

If you want to request features for the 2025 roadmap of [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io), now is the time to put those requests in.

There are two great ways to give feedback on [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io) and/or give feature requests:
1. Leave a comment below on this post. Tell us your favorite things about [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io) and maybe what you'd like to see added next
2. Post a thread on INLEO with two hashtags: #hivestats #feedback. Including these tags will help our team sort feedback and get your requests added to the roadmap for HS in 2025

Head over to [Hivestats](https://hivestats.io) and start Tracking & Analyzing your Hive Account 🦁🐝

"End of an Era (Part 452...)
I went to the bank on Friday. 

It's the same bank where I opened an account when I first came to this town 20 years ago, and the same bank that the Red Dragonfly Gallery had its accounts with, and the same bank that I've had my personal accounts with all this time.

![RD0023-Cairn.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/reddragonfly/23xepGeBHEcqzEM5kjj41aUY5wFTr85fbbLMxGFtJj31hXQNNFcePd9AaquwmeW2XxhMx.JPG)

This is an old Local/Regional bank that serves a relatively limited geographical area of Western Washington State, having been pretty stable at about 20 branches across three counties. It has actually been *owned by the same family since 1904* and managed to make it through the Great Depression, a World War, the wild inflation of the 1970s, the 2008 banking crisis, Covid lockdowns and still survived as a single banking organization run by people for people... all without government intervention, bailouts and takeovers by large hostile banking organizations.

Remarkably, my "free basic checking" account has remained *free,* all this time. 

Sadly, this 122-year-old tradition came to a close this past weekend as the bank becomes part of a larger West Coast banking organization. We've gotten lots of paperwork, along with assurances that the same faces will still be working at our branches and the same services will still be available, but I can't help but wonder how true that's actually going to be.

![RD-0012-Birds.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/reddragonfly/23wgYTPfxkZ4M3RhBbWsEJ9F8Bv3HxG3i1d9UMB1pt5arC5AMLbEsWTYZFfNApEeLhZwe.jpg)

I suppose *"little change"* might be how things work out in the short and intermediate term, but what's going to happen after a year or two when the larger banking corporation fully gets woven into the system?

I'm sure my *"no fee"* checking account is going to stop being no fee, and will be replaced by something that requires large minimum balances and monthly fees and per transaction fees and goodness knows what else they nickel-and-dime you to death with. I'm also pretty sure we are going to see the end of friendly tellers giving us a call to let us know that we should come in and make a deposit in order to avoid an overdraft fee, or to check in with us that we're really making this purchase in another town with our debit cards.

I'm also pretty sure that the customer service hotline which was always staffed by *a real human being is* now going to be replaced by an AI driven automated phone system that'll put you in perpetual phone system jail, making it impossible to talk to a person, and if you actually do get through to a person it'll be some guy who calls himself Fred who's actually talking to you from Chennai, India.

![RD0086-Forest.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/reddragonfly/23tkovccJi1oQeCKgvxnK1Vg4E3DQuQscDrDfbfWqusiCWciL3Gy7Je1497FyHsCpZcXi.jpg)

I tried to be accepting of the fact that everything changes over time and that modernizations happen and I expect the people who ran the bank for all these years probably just got tired of being in the banking business in the current economic climate, or maybe the current generation decided that they just wanted to go in a different direction. And I can't say that I'd begrudge them that!

Still, it makes me sad to see another old institution fall by the wayside as the general process of standardization and gentrification seems to take hold of yet another part of our small seaside town.
